questions.questionText: A loan of 20,000 birr is offered at 10% simple interest and another at 9% compound interest for 3 years. A financial advisor is asked to determine which loan is more expensive and justify using long-term financial behavior.
options: Simple interest loan is more expensive
Compound interest loan is more expensive
questions.explanation: Compound interest grows faster than simple interest over time.

questions.questionText: A bank offers 5% interest compounded monthly. A customer deposits 20,000 birr for 3 years. The customer wants to understand why monthly compounding produces a higher return than annual compounding even when the nominal rate remains the same.
options: Because interest is calculated only once per year
Because interest is added more frequently to the principal

questions.questionText: A borrower compares three financial options with different compounding structures over 5 years. The goal is to determine which factor most strongly influences final repayment amount in compound interest systems.
questions.explanation: Rate and compounding frequency dominate growth.

questions.questionText: A savings plan shows that money doubles in approximately 8 years at a certain compound interest rate. The investor wants to estimate the interest rate and understand the relationship between doubling time and exponential growth.
questions.explanation: Review this question for further understanding.

questions.questionText: A financial institution advertises a 10% annual return compounded annually. An investor wants to compare it with a 9% continuously compounded return. The investor is asked to interpret which is more profitable and why compounding method matters.
options: Continuous compounding at 9% may compete closely but 10% is higher
questions.explanation: Higher nominal rate usually dominates despite compounding differences.

questions.questionText: A student invests 3,000 birr at 11% compound interest and observes rapid growth over time. The student is asked to explain why the growth curve becomes steeper as time increases and how exponential functions describe financial growth.
options: Because growth becomes linear over time
Because interest is applied to an increasing principal base
questions.explanation: Compound interest applies to growing principal.

questions.questionText: A business evaluates whether to reinvest profits or withdraw them. If reinvested at 8% compound interest, the business wants to understand the opportunity cost of withdrawal over a 5-year horizon.
options: Reinvestment leads to exponential growth and higher future value
questions.explanation: Reinvestment allows compounding to generate higher future value.

questions.questionText: A loan of 50,000 birr grows to 67,500 birr in 3 years. The bank uses compound interest. The analyst is asked to determine whether the growth rate is reasonable and consistent with standard banking practices.
questions.explanation: Review this question for further understanding.

questions.questionText: A savings account offers 12% compound interest but is compared with a 10% simple interest account over 10 years. The investor wants to understand which option yields higher wealth accumulation and why time plays a critical role.
questions.explanation: Compounding leads to exponential growth over time.

questions.questionText: A borrower notices that small differences in interest rate (e.g., 7% vs 8%) create large differences in repayment after many years. The borrower wants to understand why small rate changes have large long-term effects.
questions.explanation: Exponential functions amplify small differences over time.

questions.questionText: A student is asked to explain why compound interest is considered one of the most powerful financial concepts in economics and personal finance, especially for long-term investing.
options: Because it generates interest on interest over time

questions.questionText: A financial analyst is evaluating a long-term investment where 18,000 birr is deposited into a savings scheme that offers 7.5% compound interest per annum, compounded annually. After a certain number of years, the investment grows significantly, and the analyst needs to understand not only the final value but also the impact of compounding over time. If the investment becomes 23,700 birr after 4 years, determine whether the stated final value is consistent with compound interest theory and identify the closest correct interpretation.
options: Yes, it is approximately correct due to exponential growth behavior
No, it is too high compared to expected compound growth
No, it is too low compared to expected compound growth
Cannot be verified without inflation rate
questions.explanation: A = 18000(1.075)^4 ≈ 18000(1.349) ≈ 24282 birr, so 23700 is slightly lower than expected.

questions.questionText: A company borrows 25,000 birr at 9% compound interest per annum. The loan is not repaid for 5 years due to financial restructuring. The management wants to understand the effect of delayed repayment on total debt accumulation and compare it with simple interest expectations. Determine the approximate total repayment and interpret the financial risk.
options: About 39,000 birr, showing controlled debt growth
About 38,500 birr, showing exponential debt increase
About 40,000 birr, showing linear growth behavior
questions.explanation:
A = 25000(1.09)^5 ≈ 25000(1.5386) ≈
 38465 birr, showing exponential growth due to compounding.
